instructions: Dice the onion, the green pepper and 2 ribs of the celery. Mince the 3 garlic cloves.

Pat the 1 lb chicken thighs dry and cut them into 1 inch pieces. Slice the andouille into rounds about 1/4 inch thick. Put the chicken and sausage in a bowl and toss them with 1 1/2 tsp of the Cajun seasoning.

Heat 1 tbsp of the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium. Add the sausage and cook for 5 to 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until it's browned on both sides. Lift it out onto a plate with a slotted spoon.

Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil and turn the heat up to medium high. Add the chicken in a single layer and leave it alone for 3 minutes, until the underside is golden. Turn the pieces and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more. It doesn't need to be cooked through yet. Put it on the plate with the sausage.
Turn the heat back to medium and add the onion, pepper and celery. Cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring and scraping up the brown bits, until the onion is soft and see-through.
Add the garlic, the remaining 1 1/2 tsp Cajun seasoning, the 1/2 tsp thyme and the 1/2 tsp oregano. Stir for about 30 seconds, until it smells fragrant.

Stir in the can of crushed tomatoes, the 1/2 tsp salt, the 1/4 tsp pepper and 1 tsp Worcestershire. Put the chicken and sausage back in with any juices on the plate and cook for 5 minutes, stirring now and then.

Stir in the 1 1/4 cups rice and the 2 1/4 cups broth and bring it to a boil. Turn the heat to low, cover and cook for 20 to 25 minutes, stirring once halfway through, until the rice is tender and the liquid is absorbed.
Check a piece of the chicken. You're cooking it to 175°F, so if you have a thermometer, check the thickest piece. No thermometer? Cut a piece open: it's done when there's no pink left.
Meanwhile, thinly slice 4 of the green onions and chop 2 tbsp of the parsley.
Take the pot off the heat and fluff the rice gently with a fork. Taste it. If it's flat, add a pinch more salt.
Scatter the green onions and parsley over the top. Serve with the hot sauce on the side.
method_notes: All three read versions brown andouille and chicken first, soften onion, green pepper and celery in the same pot, add garlic, tomatoes and seasoning, then cook the rice right in the pot with chicken broth. Cafe Delites, the lead, seasons the meat with half the Cajun seasoning, adds thyme, oregano, Worcestershire, hot sauce and okra to crushed tomatoes, simmers covered 20 to 25 minutes and stirs in shrimp at the end. RecipeTin Eats adds bacon and tomato paste, makes its own paprika based seasoning and bakes the covered pot in the oven, and Southern Bite simmers parboiled rice with tomato sauce and bay leaves. This one follows the lead with thighs and without the shrimp and okra, so it's the chicken and sausage version, and puts the hot sauce on the side.
